Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
Heard Mr. Akhilesh Kumar Tiwari, learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. representing the State and Mr. Shiva Priya Prasad, learned counsel for opposite party no. 2.

Instant application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been preferred by the applicant to quash the criminal proceedings arising out of Complaint Case No. 1221 of 2012 (Janardan Vs. Ashish and others), under Section 498A IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Baksha,
District Jaunpur.

sentences.text:
1 On the matter being taken up, learned counsel for opposite party no. 2 raised a preliminary objection that instant application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is not maintainable because earlier the applicant has approached this Court by means of an application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. No.
19765 of 2023 seeking quashing of the order dated 15.07.2017 passed by Judicial Magistrate,
Jaunpur in Complaint Case No. 1221 of 2012 (Janardan Vs. Ashish and others) under Section 498A IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, police station Baksha, district Jaunpur whereby non-bailable warrant has been issued against her to secure her presence.
The said application was dismissed by the coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 15.03.2024, hence the present applicant is also liable to be dismissed with heavy cost.

On putting query about the aforesaid preliminary objection raised on behalf of opposite party no. 2,
learned counsel for the applicant does not dispute the aforesaid factual aspects of the matter as objected on behalf of opposite party no. 2.

However, he submits that by means of this application,
the applicant has challenged the proceeding arising out of Complaint Case No. 1221 of 2012.

Having heard the submissions of learned counsel for the parties and perusing the record, I find that in para 25, prayer has been made to quash the impugned non-bailable warrant dated 15.07.2017 and in earlier application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. No. 19765 of 2023 also, the prayer was made to quash the same non-bailable warrant dated 15.07.2017.

I also find that it is an old matter of the year 2012 and since then the applicant is avoiding judicial proceeding adopting different modus operandi and preferred the instant second application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. on 12.08.2024 after dismissal of her first application on 15.03.2024 as noted above.

Hence, in view of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Bhisham Lal Verma vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Another, 2023 SCC OnLine SC 1399, instant application is not maintainable and is liable to be dismissed.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is dismissed.
